text:
Two examples of non-environmental effects that are improperly included in the section on environmental impacts will serve to indicate how environmental values have been compromised. First, the section includes the economic effects of ORV use on rural economies and on the ORV industry. Interior should know that these are not environmental impacts. Indeed, one of the basic purposes of NEPA is to protect public resources from private use for profit. This requires that Interior clearly distinguish private economic gain from the environmentally damaging effects of ORV use. The draft statement fails to make this distinction. It classifies economic "benefits" as "environmental impacts" along with the adverse effects of ORV use on land, air, water, vegetation, and wildlife. This gives the false impression that the overall "environmental" effect of ORV use is not so bad.
Second, the impact statement includes the "exhilarating feeling of freedom" experienced in high speed travel, and "bringing the family together" as "human impacts," a subsection of the environmental impacts of ORV use. It should be clear that NEPA impact statements require a detailed statement of the effects of proposed actions on the <u>natural</u> environment. Insofar as psycho-social aspects of the human environment are relevant to the policy judgment under consideration, they must be treated separately from environmental impacts. By classifying them as environmental effects, the Draft Statement again heightens the false impression ORV use has an overall favorable environmental impact.
